1. Mfa No.201838/2023 is filed by the Nekrtc (for short 'Corporation') and
MFA.No.201522/2023 is filed by the claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
(for short 'the Act'), challenging the judgment and award dated 10.11.2022 passed by the Ii Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and Jmfc, Bidar (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC.No.303/2021.
2.

Since both the appeals are arising out of the same accident and challenging the same judgment
and award, the same are clubbed together, heard and common judgment is being passed.

Nc: 2025:Khc-K:6520-Db Hc-Kar
3.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals briefly stated are that on 05.04.2021, at about 9 p.m.,
the deceased P.Mallaiah along with P.Mahesh was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing registration
No.TS-15/EJ-2853 from Kamkole to Chandranpally on Nh-6. P.Mahesh was riding the motorcycle.

When  they reached near Budhera village, the driver of the bus bearing registration No.KA- 38/F-1069 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motorcycle The Divisional Controller vs Nagamani And Ors on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3799985/
4 from behind.

sentences.text: As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased P.Mallaiah sustained grievous injuries, was shifted to Sangareddy Hospital and later succumbed to the injuries.
4. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
5. Upon service of notice, the respondent- Corporation appeared through counsel and filed written NC: 2025:KHC-K:6520-DB HC-KAR statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
6. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove the case, examined claimant No.1 as PW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P5.
On behalf of respondents, one witness was examined as RW-1 but no document was exhibited.

7. The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.21,80,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a.
and directed the respondent-NEKRTC to NC: 2025:KHC-K:6520-DB HC-KAR deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, these appeals have been filed.
8. Smt. Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel appearing for the Corporation has raised the following contentions:
a. Firstly, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
The rider of the motorcycle was riding the same at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the bus.
He was also contributed to the occurrence of the accident.
The Tribunal has erred in holding that the driver of the bus alone was negligent in causing the accident.

b. Secondly, in respect of quantum is concerned, even though the claimants have stated that the deceased was working as a mason and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month, they have not produced any documents to substantiate the same.

Therefore,
the Tribunal has rightly NC: 2025:KHC-K:6520-DB HC-KAR considered the notional income of the deceased as Rs.14,000/- per month.

c. Thirdly, since the claimants have failed to substantiate the income of the deceased,
the Tribunal has rightly not granted any future prospects.

d. Fourthly, the Tribunal has erred in awarding the compensation of Rs.50,000/-
under the head of 'loss of future income'.
Hence, she sought for allowing the appeal filed by the Corporation.

Per contra, Sri. Veeranagouda Malipatil, learned counsel appearing for the claimants has contended as below:
a) Firstly, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the bus.
The driver of the bus was driving the offending vehicle at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
Due to the impact, the deceased, who was the pillion rider, fell down and sustained grievous injuries and subsequently succumbed to the injuries.
Immediately after the accident, a complaint was lodged against the driver of the bus and after a thorough investigation, the police filed a charge sheet.
The Corporation has not taken any contention that the negligence was on the part of the deceased.
They have raised the ground for the first time before this Court.
The Tribunal after considering the FIR, Charge sheet and the evidence of the parties has rightly held that the driver of the bus was negligent in causing the accident.

Secondly, in respect of quantum, at the time of accident, the deceased was earning Rs.25,000/-
per month.
The Tribunal has assessed notional income of the deceased as Rs.14,000/- which is on the lower side.

c) Thirdly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD.
-v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157], 40% of the income has to be added for future prospects.

sentences.text: The case of the claimants is that on 05.04.2021, the deceased P.Mallaiah was proceeding along - 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6520-DB HC-KAR with P.Mahesh who was riding the motorcycle bearing registration No.TS-15/EJ-2853 from Kamkole to Chandranpally.

When they reached near Budhera Village at about 9 p.m., the driver of the NEKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-38/F-1069 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the rear portion of the motorcycle.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell from the motorcycle, sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
REG:NEGLIGENT 12.
Under the Motor Vehicles Act, in the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal, the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in the civil case.

No doubt,
before the Tribunal, there must be some material on the basis of which the Tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to decide for awarding compensation, but the Tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt a nicety of a civil or criminal - 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6520-DB HC-KAR case.
After all, it is a summary enquiry and it is the legislation for the welfare of the Society.
The proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings under civil rules.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

In the case of MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANR. (2018) 5 SCC 656, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as hereinbelow:
"25.

entities.text: MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANR. (2018) 5 SCC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Dulcina Fernandes, this Court examined similar situation where the evidence of claimant's eyewitness was discarded by the Tribunal and that the respondent in that case was acquitted in the criminal case concerning the accident.

This Court,
however, opined that it cannot be overlooked that upon investigation of the case registered against the respondent, prima facie, materials showing negligence were found to put him on trial.

The Court restated the settled principle that the evidence of the claimants ought to be examined by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly the standard of proof - 13 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6520-DB HC-KAR beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
13. To prove the case, claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1.
In her evidence, she categorically stated that the driver of the bus was negligent in causing the accident.

Even though the Corporation examined the driver of the bus, it has not produced any documents to disprove the evidence of the The Divisional Controller vs Nagamani And Ors on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3799985/
7 claimants.

sentences.text: The driver of the bus neither lodged any complaint nor challenged the charge sheet filed against him.
Furthermore, the Corporation did not plead that the rider of the motorcycle was negligent in causing the accident.

Considering the evidence of PW.1, the FIR, complaint, IMV report,
charge sheet, the Tribunal has rightly held that the driver of the bus was negligent in causing the accident.
REG:QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION 14.
Even though the claimants claimed that the deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- per month, they have - 14 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6520-DB HC-KAR not produced any documents to establish the same.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for accidents that occurred in the year 2021, the notional income of the deceased has to be taken as Rs.14,250/- per month.

To the aforesaid income,
40% has to be added towards future prospects, in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case of 'PRANAY SETHI' (supra).

15. Since there are four dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and the remaining amount has to be taken as his contribution to the family.
The multiplier applicable to the relevant age group is '15'.

Accordingly, the loss of dependency has to be reassessed as follows:
Rs.14,250+40%*12*15-1/4 = Rs.26,93,250/-
16.

In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.16,500/- on account of 'loss of estate',
- 15 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6520-DB HC-KAR and compensation of Rs.16,500/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.
17.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 'MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD.'(Supra), claimant No.1-wife of the deceased is entitled to compensation of Rs.44,000/- under the head of 'loss of spousal consortium'.
Claimant Nos.2 and 3, children of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.44,000/- each under the head of 'loss of parental consortium'.
Claimant no.4 is entitled for compensation of Rs.44,000/- under the head of 'loss of filial consortium'.

18. Thus, the claimants are entitled for the following compensation:

ORDER a) The appeals are disposed of.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.29,52,250/- as against Rs.21,80,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

d) Following the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of 'MS.JOYEETA BOSE' (supra), the enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6%
